items.name: axHub connector (first slice: approvals feed, hub address, locked web view)
items.description: What axHub serves today, for any AXF app: hub address rules (https host only; links checked against that exact origin), hub URLs (approvals, one approval by id, sign-in, account, app catalog), the approvals feed GET /auth/admin/approvals.json (axHub decision #85) read with the app's own hub session (web: the browser's cookie, credentials included; Android: the WebView cookie store) with redirects refused and the reply size-capped, mapped to ok / signed-out / not-admin / unreachable, seen-id tracking so each approval rings once, sign-out on the hub (CSRF form post), and on Android a web view locked to one origin plus hub APK downloads through the download manager. Web (framework/libs/hub) and Kotlin (lib-hub HubRules) replay one fixture, spec/fixtures/hub-approvals.json. The hub protocol contract (AXPP) is a named placeholder, parked for Fable. Developer apps: the same module attaches the hub appearance source (appearance@1 document on the hub's data server, live change feed, backoff, waiting screen + HubSignInView while the hub is unreachable; HubOrigin also allows localhost for dev).

params.help: https, host only (no path)

android.note: written without a compiler; CI compiles and runs :lib-hub:testDebugUnitTest (HubRules replayed the fixture with a local kotlinc)

items.name: App lock (fingerprint/face or PIN)
items.description: Second-step unlock any app can put after its own first step: strong biometrics through BiometricPrompt, or a 4–12 digit PIN kept only as a salted PBKDF2 hash in the Keystore-backed secure store. Failed PINs lock out with a doubling delay that survives restarts (PersistedLockout). LockGate opens and closes the app's screens (starts locked, auto-lock after leaving or idling, fails closed without the lock service) and Gated{} shows the locked card with the unlock step; AppShell(viewGuard) puts it around every view. The lock-mode guard puts Settings → App lock back when PIN is picked without a PIN or fingerprint without a sensor. StoredSecret + SecretKind (pin, passphrase) keep other hashed secrets such as a spoken unlock code. Settings group App lock (mode, auto-lock delay) and the lock-pin view (current PIN required to change). Fills the platform's android.biometric placeholder.

placeholders.note: Keystore keys that need the fingerprint for every decrypt (CryptoObject). Not built: the lock gates the UI. Hook: axf-platform-android KeystoreFileStore(configureKey = { it.setUserAuthenticationRequired(true) … }) + decryptCipher() for a BiometricPrompt CryptoObject.

items.name: MCP client (connect to MCP servers)
items.description: Any AXF app as an MCP client: a server registry (records in the key-value store, tokens only in the platform secure store), Streamable HTTP sessions (JSON-RPC, SSE replies, session ids, version negotiation, pagination, cancellation, timeouts), browsing tools/resources/prompts and calling tools under the kernel interop exposure rules (mcp.call / mcp.call.write / mcp.call.destructive + confirmation). Pure-Kotlin engine in the kernel (ai.amberx.axf.kernel.mcp) mirrors framework/core/engines/mcp.ts and framework/python/axf_libs/mcp; all three replay spec/fixtures/mcp-client.json. Registers the kernel's axf.remote (RemoteServices) provider.

items.name: Notifications (channels, private lock-screen alerts)
items.description: Android notifications with the privacy rules built in: channels (importance, lock-screen visibility, vibration, badge), canPost (POST_NOTIFICATIONS on Android 13+; every post checks it), canFullScreen (Android 14+ per-app opt-in), the quiet ongoing "watching" notification for a foreground service, high-priority alerts that are VISIBILITY_PRIVATE with a public version (the lock screen shows only e.g. "Approval waiting"), full screen only when asked and allowed, quiet notices, post/cancel by tag or id. Never shows the app over the lock screen. Hook for alert@1 deliveries (AlertNotifications.plan / AxfNotifications.deliverAlert, channel "device"). Fills the platform's android.notifications placeholder.

items.name: Voice (speech in, prompts out, voice commands)
items.description: One-shot speech recognition as a suspend call (on-device recognizer for secret speech when the phone has one), spoken prompts that finish before the next listen, and an open registry of voice commands. Every command ships default trigger phrases; users switch defaults off, record their own (pick from what the recognizer heard) or type them in Settings → Voice triggers. Pure-Kotlin phrase matching (normalize, fuzzy trigger + label scores) and SpokenText normalisers ("gmail dot com" → gmail.com, spoken codes as plain words) so other ports can mirror them.

items.name: Work (poll jobs in a foreground service, boot restart)
items.description: The Android host for work@1 poll jobs: an app registers a job (a kernel JobSpec: interval bounds as data, one rule per outcome with fixed / exponential / interval delays, one-time notices per spell, run conditions read from the app's own prefs, foreground + boot restart) whose body is a suspend function that only calls libraries; the loop is the framework's. PollService (foreground, specialUse) drives every job through the kernel's WorkEngine state machine and only carries out its effects (run, sleep, stop, notice, status); START / CHECK_NOW / STOP / INTERVAL commands; a refused foreground start stops quietly; START_STICKY; WorkBootReceiver restarts jobs after a reboot or update when their conditions hold; running-state + state flows per job; the ongoing notification through lib-notifications, rebuilt from the job's state after every run. Fills the platform's android.work placeholder. The engine is cross-port: framework/core/engines/work.ts = ai.amberx.axf.kernel.work.WorkEngine, fixture spec/fixtures/work.json.

android.note: written without a compiler; CI compiles and runs :lib-work:testDebugUnitTest (the kernel engine + WorkConformanceTest and JobRunner were compiled and replayed with a local kotlinc)

web.note: engine + reducer only (no timer host yet); self-test spec/check-work.mts

items.name: AshesUI (live element inspector)
items.description: A live inspector for any AXF app, switched on from the context menu (AshesUI, with a check mark while on). While on, a small headless tooltip follows the pointer and shows what is under it: framework component, active asset, the plugin or library it belongs to (and which model built it), size, colours with contrast, font, theme tokens, role. Double-click or double-tap opens a draggable, resizable inspector window: every element on screen in a tree (the selected one expanded and in view), its parameters in two tabs (Grid and Tree), live style and attribute edits with revert, copy selector / JSON / HTML, pick mode, keyboard walking, freeze, filters (all / framework / plugins) and stats. Built Oct 23 2026 (Opus).

items.name: axHub status badge (green only while settings come live from axHub)
items.description: A small badge on the banner of any AXF app: red from the start and whenever the app isn't reading its settings live from axHub, green only while it is. Each check reads the settings document from the hub with the browser's own hub session (no token, no redirects, no cache); a developer app's own hub settings source must be ready too, and an answer older than two check periods no longer counts. Tap for the connection details (state, why, last live read, an expandable More row with the answer, time taken, settings version and address, Check now). A pop-up note when it changes (next to the badge, as a toast, or off, for a set number of seconds). Settings: show, side, dot, the words in each state, pop-up, check period, hub address. It is the framework's status widget (asset status/axhub, counter hub.live), so no new asset type. No dependencies. Built Oct 24 2026 (Opus).

items.name: axHub storage (settings and app data on axHub instead of this device)

Two classes: HubSettings (one settings document, per-key changes, last save wins, can mirror the app's own Settings screen) and HubData (tables of rows; all tables on axHub, or only the ones you pick, the rest stay on the device). The browser's own hub session, If-Match versions, tables over the hub's 64 KB limit split into chunks. The hub down = an error and a state to show, never a silent local copy. Built Oct 23 2026 for the Voice notes plugin.

items.name: axHub sync (one look, settings and data for every app and device)
